## Delivered scope and claims to verify

1. **Standalone capture/replay in Rust.** `src/lib.rs`, `src/ffi.rs`,
   `include/recorder.h`, `host/`, `patches/`, `cmake/`: ordered keyboard/mouse
   polls (including empty polls and wait/take semantics), clock, initial PID,
   read-time file bytes, file-existence results and bot-key checks. Replay
   supplies external results, not engine RNG or bot decisions. Frames and
   messages are observations. Audit completeness boundaries and failure paths,
   not just the successful round trip.
2. **Small engine/recorder boundary.** C translates engine structures, renders
   read-only observations and provides forked saves; Rust owns capture,
   replay, stream/frame encoding and verification. Inventory/spell observer
   helpers remain C for engine ABI access. Inspect whether that separation is
   accurately described and whether observations mutate live state/RNG.
3. **Versioned/pinned consumption.** Compare each consumer's `recorder-pin.json`
   and full vendor file set to the released tree. Its checker is outside the
   bytes being checked and runs from Cargo/CMake. The optional dependency is
   linked through the consumer's existing Rust staticlib. No second Rust
   runtime is linked. Recorder-off C oracle/default checks remain off.
4. **Fork safety.** The host saver and both consumers' existing checkpoint
   children enter snapshot-only mode. Children must not append to parent
   streams, consume inherited buffered replay cursors or emit parent footers.
   Inspect every save/fork path, interruption and malformed/leftover-input case.
   The frequent-checkpoint regression also compares final/checkpoint save bytes.
5. **Human play and continuations.** In borg-rs, `start-recording.sh` leaves the
   Borg off until explicitly activated. Named saves/backups, character locks,
   saved RNG and separate per-launch bundles are preserved. Resuming starts
   fresh Borg memory. Existing CLI takeover remains a separate legacy adapter,
   not the new in-game branch-tree feature.
6. **Persistent storage and publishing.** `tools/recording_paths.py` selects the
   sibling player-cemetery in normal clones and linked worktrees; explicit
   `BORG_PLAY_DATA_DIR`/`BORG_DEATH_RECORDS_DIR` overrides still work. Review
   `tools/cemetery_publish.py` for scope-safe Git staging/commits/pushes,
   concurrent/unrelated edits, failures/retries, archive paths/symlinks,
   resource bounds, permission preservation and restoration. Binaries/live
   profiles stay local. Push is opt-in and never forced. Restoring verified
   replay requires the matching executable; this is not portable reconstruction.
7. **Bounded random runs.** `record-random-runs.py` uses fresh random race/class
   births, distinct named runs and explicit run/turn/key/wall limits. It uses
   the same recording/export path and opt-in publishing. It is a foreground
   bounded tool, not a cohort service or strategy experiment. No attempted
   outcome may silently disappear or be counted as an independent replay life.
8. **C retirement without losing normal tools.** The scoped C diff removes
   the recording producer/build path while retaining observer-only headless
   runs, visible play, backup/autosave isolation, final-save publication, death
   export and historical readers. C `src/` has no change in this merge window.
9. **Evidence/provenance.** Retain original donor credits and licence notices
   (`CREDITS.md`, consumer `IMPORTED.json`); distinguish default/optional builds,
   real/fixture tests, observed/inferred results and local/upstream delivery.
   Check that no current claim implies an independent review, a win rate or
   an advanced feature that has not been implemented.

These are author reports and existing CI, not this review's reproduced results.
The machine-readable evidence file records exact check status/head/links.
`docs/validation-v0.1.0.json` is a committed standalone receipt. Raw local proof
was retained under `/tmp/recorder-release-sealed`, `/tmp/recorder-gui-regression`
and `/tmp/start-recording-*`; those paths are host-local/ephemeral, not a cold
backup or a prerequisite for reproducing the tests. Use pinned source and CI
artifacts where local raw data is unavailable. State unavailable evidence.

Failures are retained in the record: the first tagged CI lacked X11 development
headers; read-only file-byte capture alone missed existence decisions; a
checkpoint child consumed/appended inherited recorder streams; the first archive
restore lost runner executable permissions; and the reborn gate initially
failed new-build death accounting. The latter's D2093/D2094 are unassessed
validation controls with matching keys/messages/state and original CI evidence,
not an improvement claim. Do not replace these failures with only green reruns.

## Limits and pending work

- Linux x86-64 initial ABI; terminal dimensions 1..255. No general platform,
  architecture, GUI-duration or completeness certification follows from the
  listed tests. Audit any claim that reads more broadly.
- Initial per-process stream-directory format and compatibility archives. No
  single-file branch tree, rolling rewind window, in-game recording switch,
  in-game scrub/menu/restart-branch workflow, WASM reader or upload site.
- Existing command-line takeover/backup branches remain separate bundles.
  A save/load is not a restoration of the live game's transient/Borg state.
- Compressed publisher exports omit binaries, cap Git archives at 95 MiB,
  require matching binaries for restore/replay and do not establish the later
  few-MB/20,000-turn portability/size target. Large release-asset publication is
  separate. No unattended publishing or batch scheduler is installed.
- Reborn has the optional engine/crate integration and test interface; it does
  not gain borg-rs's human launcher/publisher as a new default frontend.
- Strategy work, source carries, win/performance/cohort claims, pristine Rust
  engine work, later consumer versions and lab deployment are outside M1.

Known limitations are not exemptions from bugs or misleading claims in the
implemented paths. Report a concrete finding whenever the actual code or
claimed acceptance boundary is wrong.

## Review workflow

Read [the reviewer prompt](../review/M1-PROMPT.md) and
[reproduction guide](../review/M1-REPRODUCE.md). Work in isolated checkouts and
private profiles; coordinate heavy builds/runs with `/tmp/angband-validation.lock`.
Never push to a real cemetery during a review control. Do not post upstream.

The reviewer returns **approve / approve with corrections / do not approve**,
findings **M1-F1..n** with severity, exact repository/commit/file:line, concrete
failure, reproduction/read-only basis and acceptance impact, plus tests run,
skips and unresolved evidence. No reviewer result is pre-filled by the author.
Post the report on issue #2 (or link an immutable report there). If writing a
local report, `docs/review/M1-REVIEW.md` is reserved for the reviewer; this
package intentionally does not create that verdict file.

Corrections get normal scoped commits and an explicit finding-disposition map;
preserve the reviewed original input set. The owner accepts or rejects M1 after
the independent report. No acceptance tag or next milestone is automatic.
